name: Connector labels use IN and OUT while serialized port IDs stay compatible
Dragging replaces an occupied output and input in one commit
Shift input-to-output drag supports changing the source
Two-click wiring and keyboard port activation both work
A preview appears while dragging; a blank drop preserves all existing wires
Esc, pointer cancellation and invalid direction never remove original connections
Selected wire Delete and a port context click disconnect the intended wire
Wiring after Process, Recovery or completion resets the run and can be repaired and restarted
Editing an idle Flow with initial work does not start processing or lock further edits
A temporarily incomplete edit can be repaired and the Join/Fork cycle runs normally
Dragging an occupied input reconnects its existing wire to a new input
Dragging a wire itself reconnects its destination
Dropping near a compatible port snaps to it without requiring a direct hit
Removing added Join/Fork ports deletes only their wires and re-add uses a fresh ID
Router ports can shrink to one per side, clearing connections and preserving other port IDs
Fixed ports and minimum Join/Fork ports cannot be removed
Port removal during Process or Recovery resets the run and removes the port
Cancelled, invalid and unchanged wiring preserve runtime; moving and timing edits do too
Wiring while running stops the engine, restores Initial Contents and clears output data
Boundary port deletion after Start updates the same equipment and disconnects external links
Adding, duplicating and deleting Flow boundary nodes keeps equipment port counts synchronized
Loading removes a stale middle port without losing a later port connection
Context menu stays inside the editor when opened at its bottom right corner
Flow editor shows the same Start checks on open, refresh and edit
